title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
corePattern: Dummy Node plus In-Place Linked List Group Reversal
interviewTips: Ask what to do when remaining nodes are fewer than k - they must stay in original order.
Clarify edge cases k equals 1, empty list, k larger than length, and whether O(1) extra space is required.
Trade-off: counting length first is simple but needs two passes, probing kth on the fly plus in-place reversal is one pass O(1) space.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Stack Based Group Reversal
approaches.intuition: If we could hold k nodes at a time, reversing them is just popping a stack. Check that k nodes remain, push them, then pop to relink in reverse order.
approaches.theory: Use a dummy head to simplify relinking. For each group, first walk k steps to verify a full group exists. If yes, push k nodes onto a stack or vector, advance curr to next group, then pop to append reversed order after prev. Link prev.next to curr for the tail. Repeat until fewer than k remain. Each node is pushed and popped once.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each node is visited once for counting, once for push, once for pop. Total O(n) for n nodes.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Stack or vector holds at most k node pointers per group.

steps: count 2 nodes from 1, push [1,2], curr=3, pop to get prev->2->1, prev=1, 1->3
count 2 nodes from 3, push [3,4], curr=5, pop to get 1->4->3, prev=3, 3->5
only 1 node from 5 < k, break, return dummy.next

edgeCases: k > length returns original list unchanged
length exactly multiple of k reverses all groups

approaches.name: Approach 2: Iterative In-Place O(1) Space Reversal
approaches.intuition: Reverse pointers directly without a stack by standard linked-list reversal confined to k nodes, stitching groups with a dummy and groupPrev pointer.
approaches.theory: Keep groupPrev as tail of previous processed part. Find kth node by moving k steps from groupPrev; if null, done. Let groupNext = kth.next and reverse k nodes starting at groupPrev.next with prev initialized to groupNext. After reversal, groupPrev.next becomes kth (new head) and old head becomes new groupPrev for next iteration. This is in-place and single pass.

code.python:
class Solution:
    def reverseKGroup(self, head, k):
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        groupPrev = dummy
        while True:
            kth = groupPrev
            for _ in range(k):
                kth = kth.next
                if not kth:
                    return dummy.next
            groupNext = kth.next
            prev = groupNext
            curr = groupPrev.next
            for _ in range(k):
                nxt = curr.next
                curr.next = prev
                prev = curr
                curr = nxt
            tmp = groupPrev.next
            groupPrev.next = kth
            groupPrev = tmp

timeComplexity.explanation: Each node is visited to find kth and once to reverse, total O(n) time.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a constant number of pointers used, no extra stack or recursion.

steps: reverse [1,2,3] with prev=4: 1->4, 2->1, 3->2, link dummy->3, groupPrev=1
from groupPrev=1 try to move 3 steps: 1->4->5->null fails, return dummy.next

edgeCases: k == 1 no pointer change but loop still correct
remaining nodes < k left untouched via early return
single node list with k > 1 unchanged
k equals length reverses entire list
